S1-01.title: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z

fields.title: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have four customers with open invoices on today's date, named "10 Trucking" (customer A), "2 Trucking" (customer B), "A-1 Towing" (customer C) and "a1 towing" (customer D). Their names differ by a number, a dash or capitals.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Look at the header of the customer name column (the first column).
  2. Without clicking any column header, find the four customers in the list (scroll down until they load if they are further down).
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The customer name column (the first column) is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 2:

  • All four customers are listed, reading from top to bottom customer A, then customer B, then customer C, then customer D (other customers may sit between them).
  • "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" because names compare character by character.
  • "A-1 Towing" comes before "a1 towing" because capitals are ignored and the dash compares as a character.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing". Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p7-a-r-summary-date-only.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today" (Production (before)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Customers come back in no set order, and no column header can be clicked to sort." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary as it opens today")

S1-05.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere

fields.title: Two customer names that differ only in capitals keep one order everywhere
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have two customers with open invoices on today's date, whose names differ only in capitals: customer A and customer B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Find customer A and customer B in the list and note which one is higher.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu at the right of the title.
  3. Open the PDF and find the two names.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and find the two names.
  6. Reload the page and find the two names again.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The two customers sit next to each other (no other customer between them) in one order.

Step 2:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 3:

  • The two names are in the same order as on screen.

Step 4:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 5:

  • The two rows are in the same order as on screen.

Step 6:

  • After the reload they are still in the same order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. For example, "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing": the accent folds for the name order (S1-R3), so the two tie, and in the plain lower-cased name the unaccented letter comes first.”
  • S1-R2: “Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing". Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".”

Preconditions

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by ID as numbers, never letter by letter, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 2:

  • Largest number first: document C, document B, document A, still in number order.

Step 3:

  • Rows inside each aging bucket sort by Due Date, oldest first.
  • Document A, document B and document C tie on Due Date, so they are ordered by number, smallest first: document A, document B, document C.

Step 4:

  • The Due Date sort reverses, newest first.
  • The three still tie and keep the same order, smallest number first: document A, document B, document C (reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only).

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Make sure you are enrolled at both locations.
  • Make sure the report has more than 30 customers with open documents on today's date and on yesterday's date, at both locations.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with open documents at both locations.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click the "Open Balance" header once.
  2. Change the as-of date to yesterday.
  3. Scroll down until the next 30 customers load.
  4. Open the Customer filter.
  5. Tick customer A.
  6. In the Location filter, untick location B.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The rows sort by Open Balance, largest first.
  • The header shows it.

Step 2:

  • The report reloads for yesterday and is still sorted by Open Balance, largest first.

Step 3:

  • The new rows are still sorted by Open Balance, largest first.

Step 4:

  • The Customer menu opens.

Step 5:

  • Only customer A's rows remain (expand a group to see them: a filter change collapses every group), still sorted by Open Balance, largest first.

Step 6:

  • Only location A rows remain (expand a group to see them: a filter change collapses every group), still sorted by Open Balance, largest first.
  • "Open Balance" is still marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R7: “The sort is kept while the user stays on the report: changing the as-of date, loading more rows by scrolling, and changing the customer, vendor, Past due or Location filter keep it.”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4).   • S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. S2-35.title: A/R Collection: changing the Past due filter keeps the sort

fields.title: A/R Collection: changing the Past due filter keeps the sort
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with overdue invoices on today's date: one 1 to 30 days past due, and two 31 to 60 days past due with different open balances.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with customer A's group expanded.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click the "Open Balance" header once.
  2. In the Past due filter, tick "31-60 days".
  3. Expand customer A's group.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The rows in customer A's group sort by Open Balance, largest first.
  • "Open Balance" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 2:

  • The report reloads with only the invoices 31 to 60 days past due (and any credits) left.
  • Every group is collapsed.

Step 3:

  • The rows in the group are still sorted by Open Balance, largest first.
  • "Open Balance" is still marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header), story SV-11534 (Story 4, Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S2-R7: “The sort is kept while the user stays on the report: changing the as-of date, loading more rows by scrolling, and changing the customer, vendor, Past due or Location filter keep it.”
  • S5-R16: “With ranges ticked, A/R Detail, A/R Collection, A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices keep only the invoices and bills whose days past due on the as-of date fall in a ticked range, and always keep credit memos, deposits and vendor credits.”
  • S4-N1: “Changing the as-of date, the customer or vendor filter, the Past due filter or the Location filter collapses every group, as changing the date or filter does today.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-E1: “A column where every row has the same value (for example Location when each customer has one location) shows no visible change; the tie-break (S2-R4) still applies.”

The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Make sure you are enrolled at both locations.
  • Have two customers, customer A and customer B, with open documents at both locations on today's date, at least two each, with different amounts.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the Customer filter showing customer A and customer B ticked.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click the "Total" header once.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the downloaded PDF and compare its rows with the screen, top to bottom.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and compare its rows with the screen.
  6. Without refreshing the page, click the customer name column (the first column) header.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu again.
  8. Open the new CSV and compare its rows with the screen.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The rows sort by Total, largest first.

  • The PDF downloads as a file.
  • The "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.

  • The PDF holds exactly the rows on screen for customer A and customer B, in the same order, and has a "Location" column, as the screen does (two locations are in view).

Step 4:

  • The CSV downloads.
  • The "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.

Step 5:

  • The CSV holds exactly the same rows in the same order, with a "Location" column.

Step 6:

  • The rows re-sort by name.

Step 7:

  • The CSV downloads with the "Success" message.

Step 8:

  • The new CSV follows the new on-screen order, by name, not the earlier Total order.

  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Past due filter, tick "91+ days", then "31-60 days".
  2. In the Customer filter, tick customer B, then customer A.
  3. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  4. Open the PDF and read the lines under its title.
  5. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  6. Open the CSV and read the lines at the top.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Both ranges are ticked.

Step 2:

  • Both customers are ticked.
  • The chip reads "Customer: 2 customers".

Step 3:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 4:

  • The lines read "As of Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days" (menu order, not the order ticked), then "Customers: " and customer B, customer A (the order ticked).
  • The PDF has no Location column.

Step 5:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 6:

  • The CSV starts with four rows of one line each, in this order: "As of: Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: " and location A's name, then "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days", then "Customers: " and customer B, customer A.
  • The column heading row follows directly.
  • There is no Location column.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S3-R4: “Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).”
  • S3-R5: “Each export states the locations under the as-of line: "Locations: All locations" when every location is ticked, otherwise "Locations: " followed by the ticked locations' names in the Location menu's order (A to Z), separated by a comma and a space, for example "Locations: Main Shop, North Bay". Under it, only when set: "Past due: " and the ticked ranges in menu order (for example "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days"), then, for one ticked customer or vendor, "Customer: " or "Vendor: " and the name, and for several, "Customers: " or "Vendors: " and the names in the order they were ticked.”
  • S3-R8: “The CSV starts with the lines of S3-R5, each in its own row, in this order: As of, Locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor line only when set. The column heading row follows directly, then one flat table: one row per customer or vendor (Summaries) or per document (Detail, Collection, Unpaid Invoices), with the aging bucket, customer or vendor in its own column; no group header or subtotal rows; one Totals row at the bottom. Money is a plain number with two decimals, and an empty bucket is a blank cell; dates are YYYY-MM-DD.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S6-N1: “With one location chosen, the column is hidden on screen and in the export.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. fields.title: A/R Detail: the group row stays pinned under the headings
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Make sure that on today's date the report has two buckets, bucket A and the next bucket below it, bucket B, each with more lines than fit on the screen.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the groups of bucket A and bucket B expanded.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into bucket A's rows.
  2. Keep scrolling until bucket B's row reaches the top.
  3. Keep scrolling into bucket B's rows.
  4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside bucket A's rows again.
  5. Scroll down fast through bucket A's and bucket B's rows.
  6. Scroll fast back up through bucket B's and bucket A's rows.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Bucket A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • It shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count.
  • It shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row).

Step 2:

  • Bucket B's row pushes bucket A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Bucket B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: bucket A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Step 6:

  • The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

  • S4-R6: “While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. S4-10.title: A/R Collection: the group row stays pinned under the headings

fields.title: A/R Collection: the group row stays pinned under the headings
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Make sure your role has the "View and Manage AP/AR Data" switch on.
  • Make sure that on today's date the report has two customers next to each other in name order, customer A then customer B, each with more overdue invoices than fit on the screen and with a phone number and a credit term on its customer card.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the groups of customer A and customer B expanded.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Scroll down slowly into customer A's rows.
  2. Keep scrolling until customer B's row reaches the top.
  3. Keep scrolling into customer B's rows.
  4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside customer A's rows again.
  5. Scroll down fast through customer A's and customer B's rows.
  6. Scroll fast back up through customer B's and customer A's rows.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it.
  • It shows the customer group's chevron (pointing down) and its label: customer A's name and count, then "Phone: " and the phone number and "Credit term: " and the credit term.
  • It shows no amounts (the customer group's sums stay in its own subtotal row).

Step 2:

  • Customer B's row pushes customer A's row up and off and takes its place.
  • Only one group row is pinned at a time.

Step 3:

  • Customer B's row stays pinned.

Step 4:

  • The change reverses: customer A's row comes back down into the pinned place.

Step 5:

  • At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

Step 6:

  • The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row.
  • Two group rows never overlap.

fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.

fields.custom_steps: 1. Read the filter row under the title, chip by chip, left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Four chips, in this order: the date chip "As of: " and today's date (for example "As of: 10/15/2026"), the Customer chip, the Past due chip, the Location chip.
  • The date chip says "As of", no longer "Date".
  • The Customer chip reads "Customer: All customers" with a person icon.
  • The Past due chip reads "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon.
  • Both are in the resting (grey) style.
  • The Location chip reads "Location: All locations" with the location pin icon.
  • Every label matches exactly, capitals and punctuation included.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S5-R6: “The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.”
  • S5-R2: “The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".”
  • S5-R10a: “Filter choices are not remembered between visits: opening a report from the Reports menu starts on today's as-of date, no customer or vendor, Past due Any, and All locations.”
  • What changes for existing users: “The date filter is labelled "As of" (was "Date"). On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices the Customer or Vendor chip now comes after it.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

  • "The native checkbox menu: "Any" ticked, "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then 1-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, 91+ days. S5-R15, S5-N3." (caption of "Past due menu")

S5-15.title: A/R Detail: each row belongs to its own document's location

fields.title: A/R Detail: each row belongs to its own document's location
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Make sure you are enrolled at both locations.
  • Make sure customer A has, on today's date, an invoice A made at location A for $500.00 and partly paid ($200.00) by a payment taken at location B, a credit memo A made at location B and a deposit A taken at location B.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with the Customer filter showing customer A ticked and every bucket expanded.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Read the Location column of invoice A, credit memo A and deposit A.
  2. In the Location menu, untick location B.
  3. Expand every bucket and read the rows.
  4. Open the Location menu.
  5. Tick location B.
  6. Untick location A.
  7. Expand every bucket and read the rows.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Invoice A shows location A.
  • Credit memo A and deposit A show location B.

Step 2:

  • The report narrows to location A.
  • The Location column is hidden.

Step 3:

  • Only invoice A remains, with its open balance of $300.00 ($500.00 − $200.00): the payment taken elsewhere does not move it.

Step 4:

  • The Location menu opens.

Step 5:

  • Location B is ticked again.

Step 6:

  • Location A is unticked.
  • The report narrows to location B.

Step 7:

  • Only credit memo A and deposit A remain.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R7: “Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. That is the location the Location column shows.”
  • Key Decisions, row location: “A row belongs to the location of its own open document (the invoice, credit memo or deposit; the bill or vendor credit), the same location the Location column shows. Rationale: the aging reports list open documents, not payments, so a partly paid invoice keeps its own location and the filter never contradicts the column. Rejected: splitting a balance by where each payment was taken.”
  • S6-R2: “The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.”

S5-35.title: A/R Collection: a link with an unknown customer ignores it

fields.title: A/R Collection: a link with an unknown customer ignores it
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have a customer, customer A, with overdue invoices on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Customer filter, tick customer A.
  2. In the address bar, after customer A's code (the text after "customerIds="), add a comma and "Nobody".
  3. Press Enter.
  4. In the address bar, replace everything after "customerIds=" with "Nobody".
  5. Press Enter.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The chip reads "Customer: " and customer A's name.
  • Only customer A's group is listed.
  • The page address carries "customerIds=" followed by customer A's code (a long code, not the name).

Step 2:

  • The address bar shows customer A's code, a comma and "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

Step 3:

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: " and customer A's name.
  • Only customer A's group is listed: the unknown customer is ignored.

Step 4:

  • The address bar shows "Nobody" after "customerIds=".

Step 5:

  • The report loads normally, with no error.
  • The chip reads "Customer: All customers" in the resting (grey) style: with no known customer left, the link opens as if none were ticked.

Why: a link saved earlier can name a customer that was since deleted or merged; the tech plan says such a link must still open the report.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R14: “A customer or vendor ticked through a link, a reload or a Summary drill-down is named and ticked on the chip, even when it is not among the first results of the chip's search.”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D30: “URL keys asOfDate, customerIds / vendorIds, pastDue, locationIds (repeated keys written, comma lists also read); legacy customerId / vendorId read once as aliases.”

fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as user C, whose custom role has "Reports → Page Access" but not "Customers → View".
  • Have a customer, customer A, with open invoices on today's date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Look at customer A's name.
  2. Click it.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • It is plain text, not a link.

Step 2:

  • Nothing opens.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can)

  • S7-R1: “A document number is a link only when the user has the permission to open it and can open it in its own location; otherwise it shows as plain text.”
  • Story 7 Prerequisites: “A customer name on A/R Summary links to A/R Collection for a user with 'Customers → View', as today.”
  • What changes for existing users: “Clicking a row no longer opens it. The document number, or the customer or vendor name on the Summaries, is the link, as on the newer reports (Story 7).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 5 "Document links and Switch location" (board Links.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p5-links-only-where-they-can-open.png: figure "Links only where they can open" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)"
  • ar-ap-p5-every-invoice-number-is-a-link.png: figure "Every invoice number is a link" (Production (before)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "A number links only with the right permission and a location the user works at; otherwise plain text. Native link style. S7-R1, S7-R2, S7-R6, S7-R7, S7-N1, S7-N2." (caption of "Links only where they can open")

  • The rows sort by Total, largest first.

  • In this sort too, every customer appears exactly once and none is missing.

  • The chip reads "Past due: 1-30 days" and the report reloads with that range only.

  • Every customer left by the filter appears exactly once.

DATA-07.title: A/R Summary: the Totals row adds up exactly the rows each filter leaves

fields.title: A/R Summary: the Totals row adds up exactly the rows each filter leaves
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and location B, with location A's name first in A to Z order.
  • Make sure you are enrolled at both locations.
  • Have three customers with only these open documents on today's date:
  • Customer A: an invoice of $1,000.00 at location A 15 days past due, an invoice of $400.00 at location B 45 days past due and an unused credit memo of $150.00 at location A.
  • Customer B: an invoice of $700.00 at location A 45 days past due and an invoice of $250.00 at location B 100 days past due.
  • Customer C: an invoice of $900.00 at location A 5 days past due.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Customer filter, tick customer A and customer B.
  2. In the Location filter, untick location B.
  3. In the Location menu, click "Select all".
  4. In the Past due filter, tick "91+ days".
  5. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  6. Open the PDF and read its Totals row.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  8. Open the CSV and read its Totals row.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Two rows remain.
  • Customer C is gone.
  • Customer A appears once, with Location "Multiple" and a Total of $1,250.00 (1,000.00 + 400.00 − 150.00).
  • Customer B's Total is $950.00 (700.00 + 250.00).
  • The Totals row's Total is $2,200.00 (1,250.00 + 950.00).

Step 2:

  • The report narrows to location A: customer A's Total is $850.00 (1,000.00 − 150.00, its location A documents only).
  • Customer B's is $700.00.
  • The Totals row's Total is $1,550.00.

Step 3:

  • Every location is ticked again.

Step 4:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 91+ days".
  • Only customer B is listed (customer A has nothing more than 90 days past due), at its full balance: 31-60 Days $700.00, 91 And Over $250.00, Total $950.00.
  • The Totals row's Total is $950.00.

Step 5:

  • The PDF downloads.

Step 6:

  • The PDF's Totals row reads $950.00 for the Total, the same as the screen.

Step 7:

  • The CSV downloads.

Step 8:

  • The CSV's Totals row reads $950.00 for the Total, the same as the screen.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
  • S5-R8: “On the Summaries, a customer's or vendor's row adds up only their open documents at the chosen locations; a customer or vendor with nothing open there is not listed.”
  • S5-R17: “With ranges ticked, A/R Summary and A/P Summary list only the customers or vendors with some open invoice or bill amount in a ticked range; their rows show their full balances in every bucket.”
  • S6-R4: “On A/R Summary and A/P Summary a row shows the location's name when all of that customer's or vendor's open documents at the chosen locations are at one location, otherwise "Multiple".”
  • Key Decisions, row location: “A row belongs to the location of its own open document (the invoice, credit memo or deposit; the bill or vendor credit), the same location the Location column shows. Rationale: the aging reports list open documents, not payments, so a partly paid invoice keeps its own location and the filter never contradicts the column. Rejected: splitting a balance by where each payment was taken.”

DATA-23.title: A/R Summary and Detail Totals differ by what a Past due filter drops

fields.title: A/R Summary and Detail Totals differ by what a Past due filter drops
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  • Have two customers with only these open documents on today's date:
  • Customer A: an invoice of $1,000.00 that is not yet due, an invoice of $400.00 45 days past due, an invoice of $300.00 15 days past due and an unused credit memo of $150.00.
  • Customer B: an invoice of $500.00 45 days past due and an invoice of $250.00 100 days past due.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with customer A and customer B ticked in the Customer filter.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. In the Past due filter, tick "31-60 days".
  2. Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) from the Reports menu in a second browser tab.
  3. In the Customer filter, tick customer A.
  4. Tick customer B.
  5. In the Past due filter, tick "31-60 days".
  6. Click the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell (Expand all).
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Both customers stay listed (each has an amount 31 to 60 days past due), each with its whole balance.
  • Customer A's Total is $1,550.00 (1,000.00 + 400.00 + 300.00 − 150.00, the not-yet-due amount and the credit memo included).
  • Customer B's Total is $750.00 (500.00 + 250.00).
  • The Totals row's Total reads $2,300.00.

Step 2:

  • A/R Detail opens on today's date with no customer ticked and Past due on Any.

Step 3:

  • Customer A is ticked.

Step 4:

  • Both are ticked.

Step 5:

  • The chip reads "Past due: 31-60 days" and the report reloads with every group collapsed.

Step 6:

  • The rows are customer A's $400.00 invoice, customer B's $500.00 invoice and customer A's $150.00 credit memo (every credit is kept).
  • The Totals row's Open Balance reads $750.00 (400.00 + 500.00 − 150.00).
  • It is $1,550.00 less than A/R Summary's $2,300.00 in step 1, exactly what the Detail report leaves out: customer A's $1,000.00 not yet due and $300.00 15 days past due, and customer B's $250.00 100 days past due.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R18a: “For the same as-of date, customer or vendor and Location, with Past due on Any, A/R Summary's Totals equal A/R Detail's Open Balance Totals bucket by bucket, and A/P Summary's equal A/P Detail's. The Detail reports' Amount column holds original amounts and is not compared.   • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”
